STEP 1 - Scene: A small side portion of cooked leafy greens (looks like Swiss chard with colorful stems, red and yellow) on a large white square plate. Photographed from above, nearly top-down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is about 26 cm across (dinner-plate sized). Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2 for a round equivalent; the square plate is roughly 25 x 25 cm, about 600 cm^2. Using ~550 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Cooked chard/leafy greens with pieces of yellow and red chard stems. No visible oil or sauce pooling.

STEP 4 - Area: The greens cover roughly 8% of the plate (a pile about 9 x 10 cm footprint, irregular, roughly 45 cm^2 on a 550 cm^2 plate). Total food coverage ≈ 8%.

STEP 5 - Volume: 45 cm^2 x ~2.5 cm average height ≈ 110 ml gross volume (outer envelope of the pile, irregular and partly flattened).

STEP 6 - Grams: Cooked leafy greens at bulk density ~0.15 g/ml gives ≈ 17 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked chard ~19 kcal/100 g. 17 g x 19 ≈ 3 kcal. Chard stems are similar in calories (~20 kcal/100 g), so the same figure applies.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small pile of a few leaves on a large plate should weigh tens of grams at most. About 17 g and ~3 kcal is plausible for what is visible. Any cooking oil used to sauté the greens is not visible, so it is not added.
